section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains how the concept of "He gives snow like wool" relates to Yerushalayim and Tzion, representing lower and higher awe, and how the descent of the higher level elevates it.
section.t: a)
And one may add,
that the matter of "He gives snow like wool" also relates to the concept of Yerushalayim and Tzion at the beginning of the maamar.
For Yerushalayim and Tzion
(lower awe and higher awe)
are analogous to snow and wool.
For lower awe,
since the awe is from His greatness in the creation of the world,
it pertains also to the animal soul—like the level of snow that acts upon the revealed faculties,
and higher awe,
since it is from the sublimity of Ein Sof that transcends worlds,
therefore,
even though regarding the G-dly soul it is a greater awe,
it is in a manner that the awe of the soul does not act upon the animal soul
—like the level of wool,
which does not act upon the revealed faculties.
And just as the aspect of wool,
though it is higher than the aspect of snow,
nevertheless,
through its being drawn down into the aspect of snow,
an elevation occurs in it,
so too with higher awe
(Tzion),
that through the empowerment drawn from it into lower awe
(Yerushalayim),
to effect the refinement of the body, the animal soul, and its portion in the world,
an elevation occurs in it
[and this is like the principle that "great is study that brings to action,"
for through study bringing to action,
greatness is achieved in the study].
However, with Tzion and Yerushalayim,
the drawing down of Tzion and Yerushalayim is only that from Tzion empowerment is drawn to Yerushalayim
[like study that brings to action],
but with wool and snow,
the aspect of wool itself is drawn into the aspect of snow,
as explained above
(section 10)
regarding the matter of "He gives snow like wool."
Therefore, the elevation that occurs in wool through its being drawn into snow is a greater elevation than the elevation that occurs in Tzion through its being drawn into Yerushalayim,
and as above
(there)
that through the union of wool and snow, the root of the soul is revealed as it is rooted in the Awtsmoos.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the elevation of the higher through its descent is greatest when it effects a change in the lower, as in the work of teshuvah.
section.t: And one may add,
that the elevation that occurs in the higher through its being drawn down below is also in the drawing down of the aspect of snow and the aspect of wool into the revealed faculties.
For through the drawing down of the soul that is above the inner faculties
(the aspect of snow or the aspect of wool)
into the inner faculties to rectify and fill the blemishes,
an elevation occurs in it.
And so too with the inner faculties,
(intellect and emotions),
that through their being drawn into thought, speech, and action,
an elevation occurs in them.
But the main point of this matter
(the elevation that occurs in the higher through its descent below)
is when the higher effects a change in the lower,
for then also the effect of the lower upon the higher is in a manner of change,
so that the ascent that occurs in it through its descent below is an incomparable ascent.
Therefore, the main point of the virtue of the lower and the ascent effected by it in the higher,
is in the work of teshuvah,
for through the drawing down of the essence of the soul
(the aspect of snow or the aspect of wool)
into the inner faculties, a change occurs in them,
to the point of transforming willful sins into merits.
Therefore,
also the ascent effected thereby in the essence of the soul,
is an incomparable ascent.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the three aspects in the verse correspond to the service of the righteous, teshuvah of the snow level, and teshuvah of the wool level.
section.t: b)
And this is "Look down from Your holy dwelling, from the heavens, and bless Your people Israel,"
and it is explained in the maamar that the reason it precedes "Your people" to "Israel" is that the main revelation is in action,
for "great is study that brings to action," and those who perform a mitzvah transform curse into blessing,
for the main virtue of action is in the work of teshuvah that transforms willful sins
(curse)
into merits
(blessing).
And one may say,
that the three matters of "Hashem your G-d" in the verse "And He did not want..." explained in the maamar correspond to the service of the righteous
(the service of Torah and mitzvos),
the work of teshuvah of the aspect of snow, and the work of teshuvah of the aspect of wool.
For the matter of "And Hashem your G-d did not want to listen to Bilaam," that He does not initially want to listen to the accusers, is like the service of the righteous.
And the matter of "And Hashem your G-d turned the curse into a blessing for you,"

the transformation of willful sins into merits through the revelation of the supernal Hashem that transcends the chain of descent, is like the work of teshuvah of the aspect of snow—beyond the chain of descent within man.
And the matter of "For Hashem your G-d loves you,"
the essential love of the Holy One, blessed be He, for Israel, that even where "a brother, Esav, [acts] toward Yaakov," nevertheless "He loves Yaakov" specifically,
is like the teshuvah of the aspect of wool—the rectification of blemishes through the revelation of the essence of the soul, which even at the time of sin
(when he is like Esav)
is in faithfulness with Him.
